info.bio:
The Shadows fue una banda de rock and roll activa desde los años 50 hasta los 90. En 1975 quedaron segundos en el Festival de Eurovisión. Se reunieron de nuevo para una gira en 2004. Surgieron como The Drifters, banda de apoyo de Cliff Richard.

Miembros

* Hank Marvin: voz y guitarra.
* Bruce Welch: guitarra.
* Brian Bennett: batería.
* Jet Harris: bajo.
* Tony Meehan: batería.
* Brian Locking: bajo.
* John Rostill: bajo.

Álbumes

* The Shadows (1961, #1).

scenes.name: Antes del diluvio
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: La «edad oscura» del rock'n'roll: los rebeldes son sustituidos por ídolos adolescentes educados y el Brill Building devuelve el poder a los compositores profesionales. Pero en esos años se incuban la revolución futura: la guitarra fuzz de Link Wray, los bailes de moda (el twist), el rock instrumental de guitarras (Duane Eddy, Ventures, Shadows), el calipso y el primer ska, el doo-wop más inventivo (Coasters, Drifters, Five Royales), el nacimiento del soul (Sam Cooke, Ray Charles, Motown, Stax), el estudio como instrumento de Joe Meek y el surf de los Beach Boys y del «muro de sonido» de Phil Spector.

podcast.title: Backing Band for Cliff Richard
podcast.body: The Shadows were formed from former members of The Viper's Skiffle Group and became the backing band for Cliff Richard. "whose backing band was made up of former members of the Vipers Skiffle Loop."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 48: "Rock With the Caveman" by Tommy Steele

podcast.title: First Vox Amplifier Customers
podcast.body: The Shadows, Cliff Richard's backing band, were among the very first customers of Vox amplifiers. Their adoption helped establish Vox's presence in the music scene. "Vox's first customers were the guys in Cliff Richards band, the shadows."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Story of the Electric Guitar - Part 3

podcast.title: Influential UK Instrumental Group
podcast.body: The Shadows were an instrumental group based in the UK that achieved hits with pure instrumental records, playing a significant role in paving the way for rock and roll guitar bands. "or the Shadows in the UK, who had hits with pure instrumental records."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Name Change
podcast.body: The band known as "Cliff Richard and The Drifters" eventually changed its name to "Cliff Richard and The Shadows." This change occurred by Cliff Richard's 19th birthday, at which point none of the original members of The Drifters remained in the group. "By Cliff's 19th birthday, the only thing left of the original drifters was the name, and soon that would change too, as Cliff Richard and the drifters became Cliff Richard and the shadows."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 70: "Move It" by Cliff Richard and the Drifters

podcast.title: Origin of "The Shadows' Walk"
podcast.body: While performing Cliff Richard's cover of "Willie and the Hand Jive" live in 1959, The Shadows developed a synchronized dance. They started moving in unison to visually enliven the song. This performance was so well-received by audiences that they began applying these dance steps to every song, which ultimately evolved into their famous, or infamous, signature stage movement known as "The Shadows' Walk." "The audience reaction was so great that they started doing it on every song, the famous or infamous Shadows' work had developed."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: REUPLOAD Episode 71: "Willie and the Hand Jive" by Johnny Otis

podcast.title: Origin of Name
podcast.body: Formed by Harry Webb, Terry Smart, and Norman Midham, the group initially considered calling themselves "The Planet" after the launch of Sputnik. However, after researching the etymology of "planet" and discovering it came from the Greek for "wanderer" or "Drifter," they adopted the name "The Drifters," unaware of the existence of an American group with the identical name. "Inspired by the recent launch of Sputnik, they thought of calling themselves the planet, but they decided that wasn't quite right, and looked up the etymology of planet and found it came from the Greek for wanderer or Drifter, and so they became the Drifters, unaware there was an American group of the same name."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 70: "Move It" by Cliff Richard and the Drifters

podcast.title: Original Lineup Evolution
podcast.body: The initial formation included Harry Webb, Terry Smart, and Norman Midham. Ian Sanwell later joined as the lead guitarist. The lineup then evolved to include Ian Sanwell on bass, Terry Smart, Hank Marvin, and Bruce Welch. Eventually, only the name "The Drifters" remained from the original configuration before the band was rebranded as "The Shadows." "Webb and Smart left the Dictig Skiffle group, and with Midham they formed a new rock-and-roll group."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

xref.title: Untimely Death and Legacy
xref.body: Christian died young from tuberculosis on March 3rd, 1941, at the age of 25. Despite his short career, he is credited with taking the amplified guitar out of the shadows and establishing the foundational role of the lead guitarist in modern music. "Until he died of tuberculosis on March 3rd, 1941 at the age of 25, Charlie took the new amplified guitar out of the shadows and is now recognized as the person to create the foundations of the lead guitarist as we know it today."
